Article Title: Two of America's biggest AI companies are in price war, and the links go to China
Article Text:
Cuts for mid-tier AI models

Corporate budgets drive adoption of Chinese silicon

OpenAI and Anthropic – two of America’s artificial intelligence (AI) pioneers – have slashed access fees for their language models to stop budget-focused enterprise clients from migrating overseas even as they face mounting pressure from low-cost Chinese rivals. The price battle arrives as mounting computing expenses force corporations across Europe and Silicon Valley to curb their usage. This has allowed Chinese developers like DeepSeek and Moonshot to win over major business accounts.Citing Silicon Data’s token price index, the Financial Times reported that rates paid by consumers for flagship US models have plummeted nearly 25% since mid-July. The downward shift highlights a pivot for domestic developers, who long relied on proprietary, closed architectures and competed primarily on raw technical power rather than pricing.The recent US developer price cuts are mainly on intermediate products, which are designed to be as economical as open-weight alternatives. OpenAI has cut the price of access to its fastest and cheapest option, GPT-5.6 Luna, by 80%. Input token rates plummeted from $1 down to $0.20 per million, while output charges dropped from $6 to $1.20 per million.Similarly, Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5 at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, offering top-tier reasoning at exactly half the rate of its premium Fable 5 tier.Additionally, the startup abandoned a price hike on its Sonnet 5 model that was scheduled for September.The pricing battle unfolds as both Anthropic and OpenAI prepare for initial public offerings (IPOs) at trillion-dollar valuations, all while institutional backers demand clear paths to profit on massive infrastructure expenditures.Simultaneously, both US providers have moved business clients away from flat-rate subscription agreements toward usage-based billing, charging enterprises directly for the computing power they utilise. In response to rising overhead, commercial customers such as Airbnb and DoorDash have started deploying Chinese-built models to contain operational expenses.These decisions coincide with rapid advancements from Chinese labs, which have sharply narrowed the technical performance gap against top-tier American systems while allowing developers to freely download, run, and modify their model weights.
Article Summary: OpenAI and Anthropic have slashed access fees for their language models to stop budget-focused enterprise clients from migrating overseas. The price battle arrives as mounting computing expenses force corporations across Europe and Silicon Valley to curb their usage. This has allowed Chinese developers like DeepSeek and Moonshot to win over major business accounts.

Article Title: Elon Musk responds to Apple CEO John Ternus' 'Hello' message
Article Text:
AMD CEO Lisa Su , Salesforce chief Marc Benioff extend congrats to new Apple CEO

Apple’s leadership transition after 15-year Tim Cook era

Billionaire Elon Musk , and multiple other tech executives have extended their congratulations to newly-appointed Apple CEO John Ternus, reacting directly to the executive’s first-ever post on social media platform X (formerly Twitter). Making his first public post on the platform since stepping into Apple ’s top leadership role, Ternus shared a minimalist greeting that read simply, “hello”.Responding to the update, the Tesla and X chief wrote, “Congrats!"”before following up with an additional comment noting, “New Apple CEO posting on X”.Not just Musk, executives including AMD CEO Lisa Su, Salesforce chief Mac Benioff, Logan Kilpatrick , who is the product lead for Google AI Studio, also wished the new Apple CEO.“Congrats John! All the best,” said Su. Benioff added a simple “Congrats” with a heart emoji. Kilpatrick said: “good morning.” IBM posted a meme in which a person is seen waving hand in “hello” fashion.Tech millionaire Bryan Johnson posted a long message, welcoming Ternus on X, saying, “Hey John, congratulations and welcome to X.”“A heads up that you may see some unusual things from me on the TL. I'm trying to stop. Also, I see you were an accomplished rower at Penn.lmk if you want to join me in an attempt to dunk a basketball. We're the same age,” he added.Greg Joswiak, Apple SVP marketing replied to Ternus post: "Hello, indeed. More to say September 9. 😉"Ternus formally stepped into the chief executive seat on September 1, 2026, marking the conclusion of Tim Cook’s 15-year tenure leading the technology giant. The 51-year-old executive takes charge at a crucial juncture, as Apple confronts escalating market pressure to match competitors in the fast-moving artificial intelligence (AI) landscape.Ternus brings 25 years of experience to the chief executive role, having first arrived at Apple in 2001 as part of its design group. He has worked with Apple cofounder and former CEO Steve Jobs . He advanced to vice president in 2013 and was elevated to senior vice president of hardware engineering in 2021, reporting directly to Cook.Throughout his executive leadership, Ternus guided hardware engineering initiatives across Apple's cornerstone devices, including the iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch and Vision Pro.
Article Summary: Elon Musk, AMD CEO Lisa Su, Salesforce chief Mac Benioff, Logan Kilpatrick extend congratulations to new Apple CEO John Ternus. The 51-year-old executive takes charge at a crucial juncture as Apple confronts escalating market pressure to match competitors in the fast-moving artificial intelligence (AI) landscape.

The problem Jio says it's solving

Pricing and plans

Reliance Jio has launched JioPC as a standalone subscription service, making its cloud-computing offering available to anyone with an internet connection regardless of which telecom or broadband provider they use. The service, previously restricted to JioHome broadband subscribers, is now open to consumers across India who want to extend the life of an aging computer without buying new hardware. What JioPC actually offersJioPC brings cloud computing power to a user's existing device, giving them access to up to 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage without needing to replace the physical computer itself. Jio is positioning the service specifically for computers that are three to four years old and have started slowing down, running low on storage, or falling behind on operating system updates — offering an alternative to buying new hardware or paying for expensive upgrades.According to Jio, setting up JioPC takes less than five minutes, with no data migration required, no new hardware to install, and no downtime during setup.Jio frames the launch as a response to a widespread and growing issue: millions of computers in Indian homes, schools, and small businesses are aging and slowing down just as modern, AI-enabled software demands more performance than these older machines can deliver — at a moment when replacing a computer outright has become considerably more expensive.Jio is pitching JioPC heavily around AI readiness, arguing that the next generation of learning and everyday computing will increasingly depend on AI-powered tools. Since JioPC handles computing-intensive AI processing on Jio's cloud infrastructure rather than on the local device, the company says even a computer as old as eight years can access the performance and storage needed to run today's AI-powered applications — without any new hardware or upgrades, just a cloud connection.JioPC is available in two tiers, each offered across multiple validity periods:JioPC (8GB RAM, 500GB Storage):* 2 months — Rs 1,000* 5 months — Rs 2,000* 10+2 months — Rs 4,000JioPC Ultra (16GB RAM, 1TB Storage):* 2 months — Rs 1,200* 5 months — Rs 2,500* 10+2 months — Rs 5,000
Article Summary: Reliance Jio has launched JioPC as a standalone subscription service. The service, previously restricted to JioHome broadband subscribers, is now open to consumers across India. It brings cloud computing power to a user's existing device, giving them access to up to 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage.
